predecessors.name: Haryanka dynasty
predecessors.text: the Haryanka state as the magadha-haryanka-dynasty dossier hands it over at its 413 dissolve: Magadha with Anga, the Vajjika country, the Mallas and the Kosala-Kasi land

successors.name: Nanda Empire
successors.text: the whole state as it stood in 345 BCE (Haryanka land, Avanti with Vatsa, Matsya): 'This dynasty was succeeded by the Nanda dynasty in c.

ledger.x: 413 BCE: Shishunaga takes the Magadhan throne after a popular rebellion and founds the Shaishunaga dynasty at Rajgir.
404 BCE: Magadha annexes Avanti and Vatsa.
395 BCE: the capital moves to Pataliputra.
345 BCE: Mahapadma Nanda seizes the throne and the dynasty ends.

wars.name: Revolt against the Haryanka dynasty
wars.outcome: The rebels place Shishunaga on the throne; no land changes hands beyond the change of dynasty.

wars.name: Shishunaga's conquest of Avanti
wars.outcome: Magadha wins: Shishunaga defeats Nandivardhana (Avantivardhana), the last king of the Pradyota dynasty, and annexes Avanti; the page adds Kosala and Vatsa.

wars.name: Mahapadma's seizure of the throne
wars.outcome: Mahapadma, called the illegitimate son of Mahanandin, kills him and founds the Nanda dynasty.

certainty.note: All frontiers are approximate: the only map on the page is captioned 'Approximate extent of the Shaishunaga dynasty' and the text gives no boundary; the Ganga, Son and Champa lines of the Magadhan core in the Haryanka dossier are the…
